:::{#exr-row-null-disjoint-practice}
#### Testing a row-space vector against the null space

@thm-row-null-disjoint says that a nonzero vector in the [row space](#def-row-space)
is never in the [null space](#def-null-space).
Let

$$
\matr{A} = \sbmat{1 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 1},
\qquad
\vecf{v} = \sbmat{1 \\ 2 \\ 1},
$$

so that $\vecf{v} = (1, 1, 0) + (0, 1, 1)$ adds the two [rows of $\matr{A}$](linear-algebra-matrices.qmd#def-matrix-row).

Compute $\matr{A}\vecf{v}$, and check that $\vecf{v}$ is not in $\mathcal{N}(\matr{A})$.

::: {.callout-tip}
#### Hint

Multiply each row of $\matr{A}$ by $\vecf{v}$.

:::

:::
